misconceptions.description: Treating a platform affordance as a list of buttons the tool offers rather than the learner action the tool makes easy or hard
misconceptions.trigger: learner describes the LMS by enumerating features (quizzes, forums, badges) instead of the learner behaviors those features afford or block
misconceptions.feedback: An affordance is a relationship between the tool and a learner action, not a feature checkbox. Ask what the platform makes easy, hard, or impossible for the learner to do.

misconceptions.description: Reading every platform constraint as a flaw to engineer around instead of a boundary that can be designed with
misconceptions.trigger: learner proposes plugins or workarounds to defeat a constraint rather than asking whether the constraint protects a learning purpose
misconceptions.feedback: Some constraints are productive. Before working around a limit (for example, no auto-grading of essays), ask whether the constraint actually serves the learning goal.

misconceptions.description: Designing the storyboard for an idealized platform and ignoring what the actual delivery tool can render
misconceptions.trigger: learner specifies drag-and-drop branching or video annotation that the assigned LMS cannot deliver
misconceptions.feedback: Design within the affordances of the real delivery platform. Note the platform you are targeting and confirm each interaction it can actually support.
